banner: The executed operating point. Bound bytes, never an assumption.
why_this_file_exists: environment/bia_loader.py imported `gpt` and solution/reference.py imported `muon` with the comment 'shipped in the pinned image'. Neither module exists in pytorch/pytorch@sha256:db80a41f8428644cebcb3d75b0b62df334ab6c0e75785951eb25f48bfbd42407, and neither does the FineWeb shard the VOLUME declares. The modules now ship in the bundle and are COPYed into both images. This file names the shape they are instantiated at, so the executed point is a readable byte rather than a constant buried in a module.

bound.role: the point task.toml and instruction.md describe
bound.statement: One H100, the FineWeb-EDU shard Harbor mounts at /data/fineweb/train, the 124M nanogpt architecture, and the held-out split the verifier image is said to carry. No FineWeb byte and no held-out split byte exists anywhere in this bundle or in the pinned image, so this point cannot be executed from the delivered closure. It is retained verbatim, is still selectable by BIA_OPERATING_POINT=bound, and still carries the gap the bundle already declares.

demonstration.role: the point the reference is demonstrated at, and the point this bundle can actually execute
demonstration.statement: The same code paths, the same pinned harness, the same graded checkers and the same bound bar of 3.2790 nats, at a shape that fits the delivered closure. The two NUMERIC frozen axes are held exactly: batch_size stays the bound 480 and there is exactly one forward-backward pass per optimizer step. Only the architecture width, depth, vocabulary and sequence length are reduced, and the corpus is the deterministic synthetic language described under `corpus` rather than FineWeb. Every loss on the graded path is a real cross-entropy of the real harness-owned parameters on a real held-out stream the agent container never receives.

corpus.statement: An order-2 Markov language over a 64 token alphabet. Every one of the 4096 contexts carries the SAME successor weight profile under a different permutation of successors, so the Bayes-optimal per-token cross-entropy is the analytic entropy of that one profile and is not an estimate. The transition table seed is public, on the agent surface, and defines the language. The stream seed the verifier evaluates on is NOT on this surface: it lives in tests/holdout.json in the verifier image only, which is what keeps the graded split held out.
corpus.entropy_floor_nats: 3.1226889... computed analytically by bia_corpus.entropy_floor(32, 0.785). Recorded here as the measured property of the language; the authority is the function, not this string.
corpus.bar_note: The bound bar target_loss = 3.2790 is tests/golden.json's, transcribed nowhere and moved nowhere by this file.

frozen_axes_position.batch_size: held exactly at the bound 480 by environment/shape.json; the demonstration point does not touch it
frozen_axes_position.fwd_bwd_per_step: held exactly at 1; the demonstration point does not touch it
frozen_axes_position.dataset_digest: an authored constant in environment/shape.json both before and after this repair. No FineWeb byte ever existed in this bundle for it to digest, so it is a declaration, not a measurement. Unchanged.
frozen_axes_position.architecture_digest: an authored constant in environment/shape.json both before and after this repair. Unchanged.
frozen_axes_position.seq_len: NOT one of the four declared frozen axes. It is reduced here and the reduction is named.
